trace_summary.task_objective: A fixed three-hop retrieval pipeline over Wikipedia abstracts that performs exactly three retrievals and returns the concatenation of everything retrieved. The claim to verify is: 'The MTV show that was hosted by a member of this band, whom Street Music artist and American hip hop musician Defari was part of, was You Can't See Me.'
trace_summary.final_output_summary: 24 documents returned across three hops. Hop 1 retrieved documents about Defari and the Likwit Crew. Hops 2 and 3 retrieved various MTV show documents but none about 'You Can't See Me' or connecting any Likwit Crew member to hosting that show.
trace_summary.summary: The pipeline completed all three hops as specified, but failed to retrieve the necessary evidence to verify the claim. Hop 1 successfully identified Defari as part of the Likwit Crew. However, the query generator in hop 2 produced a query asking 'Which member of Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show You Can't See Me and when did it air?' which assumes the show exists and was hosted by a Likwit Crew member—both unverified facts. This query retrieved irrelevant MTV shows. Hop 3 repeated a similar query with the same failure. The core issue is that the queries attempted to verify a complex multi-part claim by asking about all parts simultaneously, rather than decomposing it into verifiable sub-questions (e.g., first finding which Likwit Crew members exist, then what shows they hosted). The retriever never found documents about 'You Can't See Me' or evidence linking any Likwit Crew member to hosting it, likely because the queries were too specific and assumed facts not in evidence.

failure_points.summary: Query generator produced a compound query that assumes unverified facts (that 'You Can't See Me' exists as an MTV show and was hosted by a Likwit Crew member)
failure_points.observed_evidence: The hop 2 query is 'Which member of Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show You Can't See Me and when did it air?' This query presupposes both that the show exists and that it was hosted by a Likwit Crew member, neither of which has been established.
failure_points.inferred_mechanism: The query generator attempted to verify a complex multi-part claim in a single query rather than decomposing it into verifiable sub-questions. A better approach would be to first query for Likwit Crew members individually, then query for what shows they hosted, or to query for 'You Can't See Me MTV show' independently to establish its existence and host.
failure_points.suggested_intervention: Decompose complex claims into atomic sub-questions. Query for individual entities first (e.g., 'Likwit Crew members', 'You Can't See Me MTV show') before attempting to verify relationships between them.

taxonomy_mappings.name: Query_Presupposes_Unverified_Fact
taxonomy_mappings.mapping_rationale: The query generator built into the query the assumption that 'You Can't See Me' exists as an MTV show and was hosted by a Likwit Crew member, when neither fact had been established in the received summaries. This is a textbook case of presupposing unverified facts in the query construction.

failure_points.summary: Hop 2 retrieval failed to return relevant documents about 'You Can't See Me' or Likwit Crew members hosting shows
failure_points.observed_evidence: The retrieval returned 7 documents about various MTV shows (MTV's Top Pop Group, MTV Showtown, 2017 MTV Video Music Awards, If You Really Knew Me) but none about 'You Can't See Me' or connecting Likwit Crew members to hosting any show.
failure_points.inferred_mechanism: The overly specific compound query from F1 likely failed to match documents in the corpus. If the show 'You Can't See Me' exists in the corpus under a different framing, or if Likwit Crew member hosting information exists separately, the compound query would miss both.
failure_points.suggested_intervention: Improve query formulation to avoid overly specific compound queries that may not match corpus documents.

failure_points.summary: Query generator repeated the same flawed query strategy in hop 3, failing to adapt after hop 2 failure
failure_points.observed_evidence: The hop 3 query is 'Which member of the Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show You Can't See Me?' which is nearly identical to the hop 2 query and makes the same unverified assumptions. The reasoning explicitly acknowledges 'there is no evidence in the passages about: 1. Which member of Likwit Crew (if any) hosted an MTV show 2. The existence of an MTV show called You Can't See Me' yet produces the same type of query.
failure_points.inferred_mechanism: The query generator failed to adapt its strategy after the hop 2 query returned no relevant results. It should have decomposed the problem (e.g., query for individual Likwit Crew members by name, or query for 'You Can't See Me' independently) but instead repeated the same compound query approach.
failure_points.suggested_intervention: Implement adaptive query generation that changes strategy when previous queries fail. After unsuccessful retrieval, try alternative query formulations: simpler queries, entity-focused queries, or queries for individual claim components.
